issues.t: Rust in rocker panels, wheel arches and frame rails
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or holes along the bottom of the doors (rocker panels) and rear wheel arches, and flaking metal under the car. Badly rusted cars can feel loose or creak over bumps.
issues.why: Water and road salt collect in the sills and seams, often because the convertible top drains are clogged. The first two generations, especially the 1999-2005 cars, rust in the rockers and the front frame rails, which are structural.
issues.next: Have the underside, rockers and frame rails checked on a lift, especially before buying. Small surface rust can be treated, but rust through the frame rails needs welding by a body shop. Keep the top drains clear and rinse salt off in winter.

issues.t: Radiator plastic tank cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the front of the car, a sweet smell, the coolant level dropping, or the temperature gauge rising in traffic.
issues.why: The radiator has plastic end tanks that get brittle with age and heat, then crack along the seams. It is one of the most common age-related failures on these cars.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and look for crusty residue on the radiator edges. Replace a leaking radiator soon; letting the engine overheat can damage the head gasket.

issues.t: Coolant expansion tank cracks
issues.sym: A hissing sound or coolant weeping from the plastic coolant tank, a sweet smell after driving, and the coolant level slowly dropping. If it bursts, the engine can overheat quickly.
issues.why: The pressurized plastic expansion tank on the 2006-2015 Miata becomes brittle with heat cycles and cracks, often between 45,000 and 120,000 miles.
issues.next: Look at the tank for hairline cracks or crusty coolant, especially around the seams. Replace it before it fails; many owners choose a sturdier aluminum tank.

issues.t: Rod bearing failure on early 2.0L engines
issues.sym: A deep knocking from the engine that gets louder with revs, low oil pressure, and in the worst case a connecting rod breaking and the engine stopping.
issues.why: Some early 2006-2008 engines have suffered spun rod bearings and broken rods. Enthusiasts suspect oil starvation in hard driving or low oil levels. Mazda revised engine parts for 2009.
issues.next: Keep the oil full and changed on time, and check it often if you drive hard or on track. If you hear a knock, stop driving right away; continuing will destroy the engine.

issues.t: Manual transmission grinds or won't go into 2nd or 3rd
issues.sym: Grinding when shifting from 1st to 2nd or 2nd to 3rd, grinding in neutral at idle, or the shifter refusing to go into 2nd or 3rd gear while other gears work.
issues.why: The 2nd and 3rd gears in early 6-speed manual soft-top cars (built before September 2016) can be damaged, especially with hard acceleration and frequent shifting. Mazda issued a service bulletin and changed the gear design.
issues.next: Have a Mazda dealer check it against service bulletin 05-001/17. The fix is a complete replacement transmission, covered under the powertrain warranty for eligible cars.

issues.t: Clutch master or slave cylinder leaks
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft or sinks to the floor, the clutch won't fully release so gears grind, or there is fluid under the dash or near the transmission.
issues.why: The hydraulic clutch uses a master cylinder at the pedal and a slave cylinder at the transmission. Their rubber seals wear and leak with age.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid reservoir (it shares fluid with the brakes on some years). Replace the leaking part and bleed the system; many shops replace both cylinders together.

issues.t: Water in the cabin or trunk from clogged top drains
issues.sym: Wet carpets behind the seats or in the footwells, water in the trunk, a musty smell, or fogged windows after rain.
issues.why: Rain that runs off the convertible top is meant to drain out through small tubes behind the seats. They clog with leaves and dirt, and worn weatherstrips or drain valves let water in. Trapped water also causes rust.
issues.next: Clear the drain holes behind the seats with a flexible trimmer line or the tool many owners use, and check the weatherstrips. Dry out the carpet fully to prevent mold and rust.

issues.t: Soft top cracks, tears or wears through
issues.sym: Cracks, splits or holes in the fabric or vinyl top, a cloudy or cracked rear window on older cars, rub marks, or water dripping in when it rains.
issues.why: Folding the top again and again, sun and weather wear the material. Older tops crack after 10-15 years, and some 2016-2017 tops wore or had loose straps and liners early and were replaced under warranty.
issues.next: Clean and protect the top with the right product, and fold it carefully. A worn top can be replaced with an aftermarket one; check warranty coverage first on newer cars.

issues.t: Power retractable hardtop stops working
issues.sym: The hardtop won't open or close, the top warning light blinks or stays on, or it makes squeaks and buzzes.
issues.why: Limit switches, bent contact tabs, the top switch or the window module can fail, and on higher-mileage cars the top motor or gears wear out.
issues.next: Don't force the top. Have a shop check the switches first; motor and gear repairs are much bigger jobs. Lubricating the seals often cures squeaks.

issues.t: Thermostat failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, a temperature gauge that stays low or climbs too high, or weak cabin heat.
issues.why: The thermostat controls engine temperature. On the 2.0L engine it is the most common cooling repair, failing stuck open or stuck closed.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the thermostat replaced. Watch the temperature gauge, and stop if it heads to hot.

issues.t: Cam angle sensor failure causes stalling
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't start, often when hot on long trips, or it runs roughly. An oil leak from the sensor area at the end of the cylinder head is also common.
issues.why: The cam angle sensor tells the computer engine position. It can fail with heat and age, and its O-ring seal can harden and leak oil.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A new sensor or O-ring is a fairly simple repair; the sensor must be set to the correct position when installed.

issues.t: Oil leaks from valve cover and seals
issues.sym: A burning oil smell after driving, oil residue on the engine, or drips under the car.
issues.why: Rubber gaskets and seals harden with age. Valve cover gaskets, front cam and crank seals, the oil pan and the rear main seal are typical leak points.
issues.next: Find the source before replacing parts. Valve cover gaskets are an easy fix; rear main seal leaks need the transmission removed, so they are often fixed during a clutch job.

issues.t: Timing belt due for replacement
issues.sym: Usually no warning; if the belt breaks, the engine shuts off and won't restart.
issues.why: The 1.8L engine uses a rubber timing belt that must be replaced about every 60,000 miles. Old belts can snap. These engines are generally non-interference, so damage is usually limited.
issues.next: If there's no record of a recent belt change, have it done along with the water pump and seals.

issues.t: Ignition coil failure causes misfires
issues.sym: Rough running, shaking at idle, loss of power, and a flashing or steady check engine light.
issues.why: The ignition coils and spark plug wires wear out with age and heat, so the spark weakens.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replacing the coil and plug wires usually fixes it. Don't drive far with a flashing check engine light, as it can damage the catalytic converter.

issues.t: Ticking noise from the valve lifters
issues.sym: A light, fast ticking from the top of the engine, often loudest at startup or idle.
issues.why: The hydraulic lash adjusters (lifters) in the cylinder head can stick or lose oil pressure, especially when oil changes are skipped. It is a well-known trait of these engines and is usually more annoying than harmful.
issues.next: Make sure the oil is full and fresh. An oil change with the correct oil often quiets it. If the noise is loud or getting worse, have a mechanic listen to rule out other problems.

issues.t: Immobilizer failure prevents starting
issues.sym: The engine cranks and may fire briefly, then dies, or won't start at all, often with the security light flashing.
issues.why: The anti-theft immobilizer system on 2001-2005 cars can fail so it no longer recognizes the key. Replacement parts have become hard to find.
issues.next: Try a spare key first. Have a shop or dealer diagnose the immobilizer; used or reprogrammed modules are often the only option.

issues.t: Clutch shudder when pulling away cold
issues.sym: The car shakes or judders as the clutch engages when pulling away, mostly when the engine is cold.
issues.why: Some 2001-2002 cars had clutch take-off shudder that Mazda addressed with a service bulletin.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer or Miata specialist about the bulletin repair. If the clutch is worn, the fix is usually done with a clutch replacement.

issues.t: Fuel pump failure
issues.sym: Long cranking before starting, stalling, or loss of power, especially on hot days.
issues.why: The in-tank electric fuel pump wears out on older cars, and the turbo Mazdaspeed models have also needed pumps.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested before replacing the pump. Avoid running the tank very low, which makes the pump run hot.

issues.t: Battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The car is dead after sitting a few days, or the battery needs replacing more often than expected.
issues.why: Owners report batteries draining, often from something staying powered after shutdown, and the small battery doesn't tolerate long parking well.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested and a parasitic draw test done. If you store the car, use a battery maintainer.

issues.t: A/C compressor failure
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm air, or there is a grinding or squealing noise when the A/C is on.
issues.why: The A/C compressor can fail internally, in some cases at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the system pressures checked. If the compressor has failed, the dryer and expansion valve are usually replaced at the same time.

issues.t: A/C stops cooling from a cracked A/C line
issues.sym: The A/C slowly or suddenly stops blowing cold.
issues.why: Engine vibration can crack an A/C line on 2016-2018 cars, letting the refrigerant escape. Mazda addressed it with a service bulletin, and some 2019 cars have had it too.
issues.next: Have the system checked for a leak. Ask the dealer about the bulletin; the fix is a new line and a recharge.

issues.t: Infotainment screen cracks or delaminates
issues.sym: A spider-web pattern spreading across the center screen, and touch functions that stop working or press by themselves.
issues.why: The glue between the screen layers breaks down, made worse by parking in hot sun. It is mostly seen on 2016-2017 cars with the silver screen frame, but later screens can also be affected.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer about goodwill help. Out of warranty, a replacement screen or digitizer may be an option instead of a whole display unit.

issues.t: Paint chips easily on the hood and front
issues.sym: Many small chips in the paint on the hood, bumper and front fenders, even at low mileage.
issues.why: Owners report the paint on the front of these cars chips easily from road debris.
issues.next: Touch up chips early to stop rust. Paint protection film on the front helps a lot.

issues.t: Clear coat peeling
issues.sym: The shiny top layer of paint turns cloudy, then flakes and peels, mostly on the hood, trunk and fenders.
issues.why: Sun exposure breaks down the clear coat over time.
issues.next: Keep the car waxed and parked out of the sun. Once it peels, the panel has to be sanded and repainted.

issues.t: Power window motor or regulator failure
issues.sym: A window moves slowly, stops partway, makes grinding noises, or won't move at all.
issues.why: The window motor, regulator or switch wears out with age.
issues.next: Listen for the motor when pressing the switch to tell a dead motor from a bad switch. Replace the failed part; regulators often come with a new motor.

issues.t: Blind spot monitor sensor faults
issues.sym: A blind spot monitoring warning message, or the warning lights in the mirrors not working.
issues.why: Rear radar sensors failed on some early cars; some were replaced under a service bulletin.
issues.next: Have the dealer check for bulletins and sensor faults. Use mirrors and head checks until it's fixed.

issues.t: Horn cover can come loose when the airbag deploys (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: The bolt holding the horn assembly to the steering wheel could break when the driver airbag deploys in very cold weather, and the part could hit the driver. Mazda recalled cars to replace the driver airbag module.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have it done if it was never completed.

issues.t: Fog light socket can fall out and overheat (recall)
issues.sym: A fog light that stops working, or a hot plastic smell from the front bumper.
issues.why: Heat and vibration could loosen the fog light bulb socket so it dropped inside the bumper, where in rare cases it could burn the bumper. Mazda recalled cars to add a retaining spring.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Don't use the fog lights if one is out or loose until it's inspected.

issues.t: Automatic may downshift suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly drops a gear and slows down sharply.
issues.why: Wrong programming in the automatic transmission control module could cause an unexpected downshift. Mazda recalled automatic cars to reprogram it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; this only applies to automatic cars.

issues.t: Underbody skid plate may fall off (recall)
issues.sym: Scraping or dragging noise from under the car.
issues.why: The skid plate and its metal bracket could come loose and drop onto the road. Mazda recalled 2016 cars to replace it.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you hear dragging, stop and look underneath.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: Rough running, a check engine light, the engine stalling while driving, or a no-start.
issues.why: The impeller inside the low-pressure fuel pump could crack and deform so the pump stops working. Mazda recalled many 2018-2019 models, including the MX-5, to replace the pump.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get it done promptly.

issues.t: Front airbags may deploy too forcefully (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms in normal driving.
issues.why: A software error in the airbag control module could make the front airbags deploy with too much force in a crash. Mazda recalled 2016-2023 MX-5 Miatas to update the software.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The update is free and quick.

issues.t: Stability control warning light may not work (recall)
issues.sym: No warning when the traction or stability control system has a problem.
issues.why: A software error could stop the TCS and DSC warning lights from coming on. Mazda recalled 2024-2025 cars to replace the DSC unit.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the unit replaced.

issues.t: Headlight system malfunction warning
issues.sym: A message saying the headlight system has a malfunction, sometimes after driving on a slope, and headlights that no longer swivel or level correctly.
issues.why: Owners report repeated faults with the adaptive (swiveling) headlights, sometimes coming back after headlights were replaced.
issues.next: Have the dealer read the codes and check the leveling sensor and headlight units under warranty. Keep records of each repeat visit.
